tagline: Rajasthan's 'Pink City' dazzles with the Hawa Mahal, hilltop Amer Fort, the City Palace and bazaars full of textiles, gems and crafts.
overview: Jaipur, the capital of Rajasthan, was founded in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II as one of India's first planned cities, laid out on a grid. In 1876 the old city was painted pink to welcome the Prince of Wales, and it has been the Pink City ever since; it is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The Hawa Mahal, or Palace of the Winds, has 953 small windows that let royal women watch street life unseen. The City Palace is still partly home to the royal family, and next to it Jantar Mantar holds giant astronomical instruments, including one of the world's largest stone sundials.

Just outside town, Amer Fort climbs a hillside above Maota Lake, with mirrored halls and ramparts linked to Jaigarh and Nahargarh forts. Jaipur's bazaars sell block-printed textiles, blue pottery and gems, and it is part of the Golden Triangle with Delhi and Agra.
